---
applyTo: "src/utils/**"
---

<scope>
`src/utils/` is the shared helper layer used by core workflow execution, harness integrations, the VS Code shell, the standalone CLI, and a few webview-safe helpers. Keep utilities here focused on reusable behavior or single-source-of-truth constants/helpers, not feature-specific orchestration.
</scope>

<architecture>
This folder has a few important seams:

- **Config and runtime boundaries:** `ConfigurationUtils` is the compatibility facade over `CtrlYokeConfigService`; `CONFIG_KEYS`, `CONFIG_SCOPE`, and `PATH_CONSTANTS` are the canonical constants consumed across the app. Core code should read settings through these helpers, not through ad hoc VS Code config access.
- **Execution-property resolution pipeline:** `PropertyResolver` resolves prompt/workflow/settings precedence, `VarSubstitutor` applies `{{var}}` expansion after resolution, and `SessionResolver` decides whether a step reuses a session. These files define workflow inheritance semantics, so changes here ripple widely.
- **Prompt/context expansion pipeline:** `FileReferenceParser` parses `@`, `#selection`, `#sym`, `~`, and inline `$...` refs; `AttachmentBuilders` and `ContextExpander` turn the non-native ones into XML/context payloads; `PriorContextPreviewBuilder` must stay aligned with the live injection format by using the same builder path as runtime execution.
- **Discovery and file-management helpers:** `HarnessDirectoryUtils` is the single source of truth for where harness/user/workspace agent and skill files live. `AgentDiscovery`, `SkillDiscovery`, and `HarnessFileManager` should build on it rather than re-encoding paths or extensions.
- **MCP config stack:** `McpConfigPaths` knows where each harness stores MCP config, `McpDiscoveryUtils` reads external configs plus the public registry, `McpRegistryFileManager` manages ctrlyoke's own registry files, and `HarnessMcpExporter` projects the same server definition into each harness's native file format. Keep those responsibilities separate.
  </architecture>

<criticalPatterns>
- **`PathCasing.ts` is the only place that may reason about Windows drive-letter case, and its three helpers point in different directions on purpose.** VS Code canonicalizes drive letters to **lowercase** (`Uri.fsPath` is documented to yield `c:/other`, and re-applies it on every `Uri` round-trip), while Node, git, and shells report OS-native `C:`. Never try to make one casing win internally — that fights a normalization VS Code re-applies at ~110 `.fsPath` reads. Instead: (1) **compare** with `pathsEqual`/`isPathWithinDirectory`, which case-fold on win32 (matching NTFS) — these are allowlist checks, so case-sensitivity only ever produced false _denials_, and folding preserves string length so prefix-slicing callers stay correct; (2) **canonicalize to uppercase only where a path leaves ctrlyoke for another process** (`canonicalizeDriveLetter`, wired into `CliProcessManager.spawn` and `PtyProcessManager.spawnPty`) — some tools key internal caches off the cwd string, and a lowercase-drive cwd made Vite/Vitest resolve a _second_ copy of the `vitest` package, so all 114 UI suites failed at `describe()` with "Vitest failed to find the runner"/"reading 'config'" while `npm test` from a terminal passed (`c8` has the same sensitivity — see `test.instructions.md`); (3) **lowercase only for serialized content** (`lowercaseDriveLetter`, used by `CopilotNotificationMonitor`) so tracked generated files don't churn. Before this was consolidated the same case-folding had been re-derived privately four times; add new call sites here rather than a fifth. Note the stdin mode on spawned scripts is unrelated — that failure reproduces identically with `"ignore"`, `"pipe"`, and `"inherit"`.
- Preserve **`null` vs `undefined` inheritance semantics** in resolver-style utilities. In this codebase, `null` usually means “explicitly disable inherited value” while `undefined` means “keep inheriting/fall back”. This is exactly why **`??` is the wrong operator for a step→workflow fallback**: it treats an explicit `null` as absent and silently re-inherits the value the author disabled. Use `step.x !== undefined ? step.x : workflow.x` (what `select()` in `src/types/ExecutionPropertyResolver.ts` does) whenever a property supports `null`-clearing.
- **`FileReferenceParser.maskFencedCodeBlocks()` is the single mask for every prompt-reference trigger char (`@#~!$/`), and every trigger parser masks internally rather than requiring its callers to remember to.** `parseAtReferences`, `parseSelectionReferences`, `parseSymbolReferences`, `parseGitChangeReferences`, and `parseInlinePriorContextRefs` (all in this file) and `CtrlYokeSlashTokens.scanCtrlYokeSlashTokens` each call `maskFencedCodeBlocks` on their own input as the first line of the function — none of it is the caller's job. This was originally per-caller (`ContextExpander` masked before calling, everyone else forgot), which is exactly how two real bugs shipped: a diff/log excerpt's literal `<!DOCTYPE>` parsed as a `!DOCTYPE` secret grant and hard-failed `preflightWorkflowSecrets` before the harness started, and separately `$previous`/`/skill:`/`/mcp:` inside a fenced block still triggered real prior-context injection or force-attachment because `parseInlinePriorContextRefs`/`scanCtrlYokeSlashTokens` had no masking at any call site (including the editor's own token-count hook, `useAttachmentTokenCount`, which is why the displayed token count didn't respect fencing either). Moving the mask inside the parser closes this for every consumer at once — completions, chips, links, runtime injection, force-attach, and token counting all agree by construction. When a new trigger char is added anywhere in the prompt-reference system, add it to the one regex in `maskFencedCodeBlocks`, not to per-caller masking.
- **`SecretResolver.getDeclaredSecretGrants()` is the only supported way to ask what secrets a step may read.** It is the second implementation of `secrets` precedence — `ExecutionPropertyResolver.resolveSecrets()` serves resolved-property consumers, while this one serves the execution path because it must also union the inline `!NAME` grants that never appear in the declaration array. Both `preflightWorkflowSecrets` and `WorkflowExecutor`'s injection route through it, so a new consumer that reads `step.secrets`/`workflow.secrets` directly is a third precedence implementation and will drift. It already did once: the original used `??` and re-inherited workflow grants for a step declaring `secrets: null`, injecting a credential the step had opted out of.
- `SessionResolver` is intentionally strict about **same-harness-only** session reuse. Numeric `sessionId` references are 1-based prompt numbers, and the `"finalStep"` sentinel is a distinct resume path; do not loosen these rules casually.
- Keep shared runtime helpers truly shared. Files like `promptPathUtils`, `RangeNotationParser`, `ErrorUtils`, and `TypedEmitter` are safe to use outside the VS Code extension host; avoid introducing `vscode` or heavyweight Node-only dependencies into utilities that are consumed by the CLI or webview-safe code paths.
- `WorkflowLockManager` and `FileLockUtils` solve different problems: workflow runner ownership uses one `.runner.json` heartbeat file per lineage in run storage, naming the exact executing `RunRef`, while `FileLockUtils` is a generic `.lock` wrapper for cross-process file mutation (used by `TimelineRecorder` and `WorkflowLineageRepository`'s descriptor writes). `FileLockUtils` intentionally uses `console.warn` instead of `Log` because it is used by the MCP server too. `WorkflowLockManager.acquireLock` is a true exclusive create (`fs.open(path, "wx")`) with a bounded retry against a stale owner (dead PID or heartbeat older than 30s); every lock carries a random `ownerToken`, and `updateHeartbeat`/`releaseLock` both verify it first, so a stale process can never touch a successor's lock. `WorkflowPaths.ts` is the only place allowed to construct a `.runs` path from raw parts — new utilities under this folder that need one should call it rather than joining path segments themselves. Anything imported transitively by `mcp-server.ts` (which includes `WorkflowPaths.ts` and `WorkflowLineageRepository.ts`) must stay `vscode`-free — use `console.warn`/`console.error`, never `Log`.
- `WorkspaceSnapshotService` is deliberately conservative: prefer git-backed snapshots when possible, exclude artifact directories (including `.ctrlyoke`), and avoid loading large/binary files fully into memory. Keep undo/redo semantics stable when changing snapshot behavior.
- **Multi-repo snapshots**: `captureWorkspaceState`/`computeSnapshotChanges`/`undoFiles` take an optional `namedRoots: ResolverWorkspaceFolder[]`. With ≤1 named root the service runs the single-root path **byte-identically** (one `RawWorkspaceSegment` with `prefix: ""`, `pathspec: ""`) — preserve that invariant. With multiple roots it captures one segment per root via the shared `discoverRepos()` (git roots scoped to the root's subtree by `pathspec`, non-repo roots via filesystem walk); `SnapshotFileChange.path` is folder-name-prefixed (`root2/src/x.ts`) and tagged with `repo` (the prefix), and `WorkspaceSnapshot.repos` (`SnapshotRepoInfo[]`) carries per-repo `root`/`headCommit` so `enrichSnapshotBeforeContent` hydrates large git-clean files against the right repo (no `namedRoots` needed at enrich time — it reads `snapshot.repos`). Prefix ⇄ path conversions (`segmentViewerPath`, `gitRelFromChange`) delegate to `WorkspaceViewerPath.ts` (`src/platform/`) primitives (`stripViewerPrefix`/`joinViewerPath`) — the single source of the folder-name-prefix convention — rather than re-slicing prefixes inline. Undo resolves prefixed paths through `resolveNamedRelativePath` (re-exported from the same module) and guards traversal against every trusted root. The commit-range pass (`getCommitRangeChanges`) must be scoped by `pathspec` and de-duped via git-relative `seenSegmentPaths` — those seen keys include the deleted-loop's committed-clean paths, or the commit range double-reports them. Callers thread `namedRoots`: `WorkflowExecutor` from `WorkflowExecutionContext.namedWorkspaceRoots` (set in `WorkflowInstance` from `platform.getNamedWorkspaceRoots()`), and `UndoRedoCoordinator` from `getVsCodeNamedWorkspaceRoots()`. The webview undo-instruction builder is unchanged — it passes `SnapshotFileChange.path` straight through.
- `WorkspaceRepoDiscovery.ts` is the single source of repo identity shared by the hosted SCM server and the snapshot layer. `discoverRepos()` probes each root's git toplevel concurrently and dedupes to one `WorkspaceRepo` per repo; `mapRootPrefixesToRepos()` (server-only) maps each root's folder-name prefix → repo id by containment (mirroring `requireRepoRootForPath`), so the client can associate a viewer path with a repo without guessing from `label`/`id`.
- `PromptFileSplitter` and `TempFileManager` are coupled to harness limitations. Splitting prefers whole `<attachment>` blocks, and temp files in `.ctrlyoke/temp/` use category-specific names because downstream debugging and cleanup rely on those conventions.
- ctrlyoke-owned agent/skill directories under `.ctrlyoke/` are intentionally **exclusive** to ctrlyoke so harness-native scrapers do not duplicate the same instructions/context. Discovery helpers dedupe overlapping directories on purpose; preserve that behavior.
- `ContextExpander.expandContextSplit()` and `ContextExpander.sanitizeReferences()` are two independent passes over the same prompt text, run separately in `HarnessIntegration.buildPromptSections()` — do not assume fixing one fixes the other. `expandContextSplit` extracts refs into separate `directFileRefs`/`excerptContent`, but the raw `@path`/`#sym:`/`#selection:` token stays untouched in the returned `userPromptText`. That untouched token only stays harmless when a corrected reference is appended elsewhere (the "using these file references" categorized clause, or an excerpt attachment's resolved-path description) — both of which are skipped by `CliPromptPreparer`'s simple-prompt/inject fast paths (they send `userPromptText` verbatim with no categorized clause). `sanitizeReferences()` closes that gap by rewriting the literal ref token in place: folder-name-prefixed paths (multi-root) become resolved absolute paths when `effectiveAbsolute` is true, and `formatFileRef` lets a CLI provider apply its own `@`-handling (e.g. Codex's `formatFileReference` strips the `@` — routed via `HarnessIntegration.formatInlineFileReference()`, which `CliIntegration` overrides to reuse the same provider hook as `formatDirectFileRef`/`formatTempFileRef`). Directory refs (`@dir/`) are deliberately excluded from `sanitizeReferences` — they always route through `expandContextSplit`'s excerpt pipeline (never the fast paths), so there's no literal-text gap to close for them.
- **Allowed external file roots** (`dev/backlog/ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_FILE_ROOTS_PLAN.md`, implemented): `ContextExpander`/`AttachmentBuilders` were deliberately left untouched internally — both already trust everything in their `trustedRoots`/`additionalTrustedRoots` list via `isPathWithinAnyDirectory`, so external-root support is just callers (`HarnessIntegration.buildPromptSections`, `PromptEditorSupportService.handleAttachmentTokenCountRequest`) widening that list with `ConfigurationUtils.getEffectiveApprovedExternalFileRoots(workspaceIdentity)` before constructing the expander. Do not add a second containment branch inside `ContextExpander` for "external" vs "workspace" — there is deliberately no such distinction at that layer. `src/utils/FileAccessPolicy.ts#evaluateFileAccess` is the layer that *does* need the three-way distinction (workspace / trustedExternalRoot / outsideTrustedRoots), and is used only by call sites that pick different UX per case (`PromptEditorSupportService.handleOpenFile`, `PromptLinkProvider`, the `ctrlyoke.confirmExternalFileTrust` command) — it's a pure comparator and does not read the trust store itself, so effective roots must be resolved by the caller first.
- **`ModelPricing.ts` has no hand-typed price table for any harness** (as of 2026-08-21). Every harness (Copilot/Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Qwen/Antigravity) is priced by `getModelPricingFromRegistry()` in `ModelPricingRegistry.ts`, which matches ctrlyoke's internal model IDs against `src/utils/generated/modelPricingRegistryData.json` — a trimmed, cost-fields-only snapshot of the full [models.dev](https://models.dev) registry, regenerated by `scripts/sync-model-pricing.mjs` (`npm run chores -- --task sync-model-pricing`) and committed to the repo. This is a build-time-only fetch — the JSON is `import`ed normally, never fetched over the network at runtime (cost estimation stays offline by design). Do not add per-model dollar amounts back into `ModelPricing.ts`; if a model's price is missing or wrong, re-run the sync script or fix the matching logic in `ModelPricingRegistry.ts`, not by hand-typing a rate. Claude CLI's short aliases (`sonnet`/`opus`/`haiku`/`fable`) are resolved to whichever version of that family is newest in the registry at sync time — there is no pinned "current version" to update by hand either.
</criticalPatterns>
